correctness.rationale: For each positive-drift finite signed edge weighting the crossing index has exponential tail via a bounded finite-state Poisson martingale and Azuma inequality. Conditional variance of physical time equals the accumulated conditional holding-time variances plus variance of the accumulated means. A second Poisson corrector yields the exact stopped boundary term; optional stopping is justified by finite expected crossing index and bounded increments. For mean-dwell weights the overshoot lies in a fixed bounded interval, proving sharp asymptotic saturation. A 3-state Gamma example passed 24 exact rational recurrence checks; those checks supplement rather than substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: An explicit 2024 semi-Markov open hypothesis is resolved under natural finite-state finite-second-moment assumptions. The same argument yields a stronger non-asymptotic all-flux inequality with a computable flux-independent correction and identifies a sharp attainable precision limit for semi-Markov first-passage clocks, including non-exponential waiting and signed edge marks. The one-state renewal example proves the coefficient cannot be improved universally.
